expected_minimum_issues.signal: small project pipeline is generalized to all firms and all industrial clusters
three projects that entered fit-out are reversed into three projects that did not enter fit-out
rent relief is treated as the sole cause of signing and future cluster formation
two parks are ranked using different business types, metrics, and time windows
delayed entry is used to accuse firms of seeking policy benefits
a precise occupancy outcome is asserted without a model, horizon evidence, or assumptions
policy effects are asserted before the applicable policy text is obtained
the topic brief's multi-variable test is replaced by a deterministic single-cause thesis

expected_reconstructed_thesis.neutral_question: Does rent relief improve only early conversion, or does it also improve production and long-term retention?
expected_reconstructed_thesis.core_hypothesis: Rent relief may improve early conversion, while long-term retention also depends on operating inputs, customer access, and labor availability.
required_falsifiers: retention remains higher after incentives expire under comparable operating conditions
parks without incentives show equal or better conversion after controlling for firm stage
production, employment, and renewal fail to follow signed intentions
